inputs.name: Nunney K, u and reported intervals

day.reading: Nunney confirms hard selection imposes the cost and that directional change makes hard selection dominate (H2 q3); soft relief is limited to intraspecific competition (H2 q5); at M = 0.1 a population dies faster than 1 per 300 (H2 q4)
day.holds: at M < 1/2 the reported intervals are 300-700 and R4 H3 gives D 39-163 at M <= 0.03, above Haldane's 30

critic.reading: the cost is not a general bound: it needs hard selection (H2a q1), shrinks at M > 1/2 (H2 q1) and with standing variation (H2a q2); Keightley reads U = 2.2 as intolerable under hard selection (H7 q1)
critic.holds: at M > 1/2 the reported intervals are 5.7-20 generations, 15-52x faster than 300; D falls with p0; R4 H3 gives D 6.5-22 at M >= 0.1

notes: Model choice, not settled by arithmetic. The held numbers fix the structure of Nunney's result: M = 2Ku (0.1 at K = 1e4, u = 5e-6; M = 1/2 needs K = 50,000), tolerable intervals that rise monotonically as M falls, below 300 for M > 1/2 and at or above it below. Which side applies to ancestral humans turns on two inputs no held source gives: human M (K and per-locus beneficial u) and the hard/soft split (claim file H2a; L2 brackets h at 0.125-0.641 but h is not M). C_0(M) and C_1(M) are not held as formulas, so no threshold is computed. R4 H-C2's '9.2 to 27.8' for 2 ln(1/p0) has an upper end 0.6% above the closed form (27.63); its '278' would be 276.
